name: Medical documentary reel — 113 reference
method: Local frame inspection at four-second intervals, plus selected one-second detail samples. Intervals below are approximate observations, not a frame-accurate edit decision list. Audio/music/SFX were not assessed.
alignment: Do not transfer after timecodes directly to another source. Opening imagery differs; durations differ by 1.51 seconds. Ground each treatment in the new transcript.

examples.observed: Named-person images above presenter; opening text gives the name visual priority. Different images replace one another while presenter remains visible.
examples.requirement: Correct identified person and contextual source, never a generic stock person.

examples.observed: Full-screen contextual imagery of medicine-related subject matter with small subtitles.
examples.requirement: Concrete subject/action match; distinguish illustrative imagery from proof of the reported incident.

examples.observed: Medical-themed canvas, Indian Express masthead, article headline/body and yellow highlighted passage. Card builds across sampled frames.
examples.requirement: Verified article source, faithful title and supported excerpt, highlight the relevant sentence; allow time to read.

examples.observed: Extended presenter-led explanation with short green-background yellow subtitles.
examples.requirement: Retain presenter where explanation matters; no rigid requirement to interrupt every few seconds.

examples.observed: Full-screen pills then medicine vial imagery during molecule/dose/purity/potency discussion.
examples.requirement: Sequence complementary concrete views on spoken concepts, rather than repeat one generic hospital image.

examples.observed: Medicine/handcuff imagery in upper panel, presenter below.
examples.requirement: Preserve presenter while illustrating the concept; generic stock is not evidence of a particular crime.

examples.observed: Closer presenter framing and larger yellow phrase precious treatment time, separate from normal subtitle styling.
examples.requirement: Short phrase with visual hierarchy and gentle push-in; avoid duplicating the same text as two captions.

examples.observed: Second article on the same medical canvas, publisher masthead and yellow highlight.
examples.requirement: Reuse the visual design, but fetch the correct source for each distinct claim.

examples.observed: Alternation among presenter, named-person imagery, topical full-screen footage and split-screen illustrations.
examples.requirement: Choose identity, context or illustration explicitly; match action and local context.

examples.observed: Large numbered medicine-verification checklist builds over presenter: source, batch number, authenticity.
examples.requirement: Keep earlier steps visible while revealing the next step on speech; requires a true checklist renderer.

examples.observed: Full-screen phone/QR-code example during scanning instruction.
examples.requirement: Show the requested action and object together; do not substitute an unrelated phone portrait.

examples.observed: Large TEST keyword over presenter as a comment call to action.
examples.requirement: Use the actual spoken CTA keyword; never carry TEST into unrelated videos.

examples.observed: Portrait, medical background and social handle end card.
examples.requirement: Use the project owner’s supplied portrait/handle/branding, not the reference identity by default.

rules: Understand the audience question and narrative function before searching media. More asset count is not equivalent to a finished reel.
Plan mixed treatments across the whole reel: identity, context, evidence, demonstration, presenter, emphasis, checklist, CTA and outro as the dialogue warrants.
Keep ordinary captions readable and visually subordinate. Important-line typography is a separate layer, not a paragraph-sized subtitle.
Observe existing captions, split screens, article cards, emphasis text and branding; preserve useful existing edits and avoid covering or duplicating them.
Use split screen when audience should see speaker and illustration together; full-screen cutaways when detail needs the frame.
Duration follows speech and reading demand; no universal one-second ceiling. Do not insert arbitrary effects solely to meet a count.
Named identities and evidence require verified specific sources. Pexels/Pixabay are for illustration, not impersonating named people or proving news claims.
Article backgrounds can be thematic, but headlines, quotations, dates, logos and numbers must be sourced. Missing sources remain explicit requirements.
Checklist and outro are distinct treatments. If their renderer or required assets are missing, report the gap instead of silently substituting big text.
Subtle pan/zoom, transitions and emphasis must follow timeline time. Finish checks include readable subtitles, source attribution, face-safe placement and complete closing beat.
